text.arabic_uthmani: وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَلَيَعْلَمَنَّ ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ

words.gloss_range: opening connector that can either coordinate with the prior ayah or resume a fresh oath-register declaration
words.prose: The opening {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the prior scene (29:10) in reach while also allowing a solemn restart. It does not merely add another statement; it launches the first half of a doubled oath architecture whose second launch will mirror it inside the ayah.

topics.headline: boundary connector into sworn declaration
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens as an answer or continuation to the prior pressure, not as a detached maxim.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar allows coordination or resumption, and both readings keep the first connector tied to the oath clause that follows.

topics.headline: first launch of a two-part oath frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the first connector as the opening beat of a paired sorting structure that will return at mid-ayah.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence marks two coordinated verbal assertions, and the later repeated connector plus oath particle confirms the internal pairing.

words.gloss_range: oath-emphasis particle prefixed to the first imperfect verb, not a prepositional or purposive particle
words.prose: The first {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) turns the coming verb into sworn certainty rather than ordinary report. Its force is local to the first classification beat, yet the same particle will be repeated for the second beat so neither group is treated as an afterthought.

topics.headline: oath particle, not preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first knowing clause is sworn and emphatic before its subject or object is named.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as oath emphasis in the full emphatic construction with the heavy final emphasis on the verb.

topics.headline: first half of repeated oath apparatus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first particle is designed to be echoed, making the two object classes equally exposed to divine certainty.
topics.reason: The second oath clause repeats the same construction, so the first particle begins a balanced frame rather than a one-off intensifier.

words.gloss_range: sworn future-certain knowing that functions as distinguishing or classifying the first object, not mere neutral awareness
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes knowing, recognizing, teaching or informing, and the sign or mark field; local Form I verb selects knowing that marks or distinguishes
words.prose: {{ar:يَعْلَمَنَّ}} ({{tr:yaʿlamanna}}) is the ayah's first active predicate of classification, completing a subject-object judgment before the second clause begins. The oath frame and heavy ending make the knowing future-certain, while the root's mark-and-knowledge field lets knowing function as distinction. The Form I shape keeps the act as divine cognition itself, not merely informing someone else. The wording also resumes a testing-and-knowing pattern within the surah (29:3) and intensifies the wider testing formula (3:140).

topics.headline: imperfect made certain by oath emphasis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is not a loose habitual present but a guaranteed realization inside the testing discourse.
topics.reason: The lām plus heavy emphasis on the imperfect licenses the future-certain force described in the QAC grammar.

topics.headline: knowledge that marks and distinguishes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees divine knowing as the act that makes the two human classes legible, not as passive awareness.
topics.reason: V4 supports both knowing and mark branches for the root, while the local transitive verb selects knowing and the opposed object frame narrows that knowing into distinction.

topics.headline: Form I cognition rather than notification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the text keeps the event inside divine knowing instead of shifting to an announcement made to others.
topics.reason: The local form is the simple cognition verb, and no local Form IV notification construction is present.

topics.headline: testing formula becomes classification
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects this sworn knowing to the testing-and-knowing pattern already in the surah (29:3) and to the wider testing formula (3:140).
topics.reason: The rows give concrete references, and the local clause uses the same emphatic knowing predicate inside a test-to-classification movement.

topics.headline: first complete judicial beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first verb forms a complete classification beat before the second clause begins.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence gives this verb an explicit subject and object, making the first clause complete before coordination.

topics.headline: created-world branch controls the local verb
topics.blocking_evidence: V4 separates the created-realm branch into different lexical units, while the local surface is a transitive cognition verb in an oath frame.
topics.reason: The root-family association may be historically interesting, but it does not govern the local Form I verb or add a reader-facing payoff here.

words.gloss_range: the explicit nominative divine proper name serving as subject of the first knowing verb and carried into the second
words.root_gloss_range: divine-name and deity/worship field with debated derivational pressure; local use is the fixed proper name, not a generic deity noun
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) is named after the emphatic verb, so the predicate strikes first and then the agent is installed explicitly. The fixed proper name prevents a generic deity reading and gives the predicate its named divine authority. The proper name fixes one divine subject for both clauses; when the name is omitted in the second half, agency is already secure and attention moves to the changed object. Across the boundary, the prior question about divine knowledge (29:10) becomes present oath-governed agency.

topics.headline: nominative subject fixes agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that divine agency is grammatically installed before the two groups are sorted.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks this word as the explicit subject of the first knowing verb.

topics.headline: fixed proper name, not generic deity term
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the subject as the singular named divine agent, while derivational debates remain only background gravity.
topics.reason: The local grammar and QAC entry select the fixed proper name; missing V4 root rows do not negate the derivational pressure, but they also do not license replacing the proper-name function.

topics.headline: one named subject governs both clauses
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second clause can omit the name because the first clause has already fixed the agent for the whole binary judgment.
topics.reason: The second verb has an implicit subject while the first clause supplies the explicit divine subject.

topics.headline: prior divine knowledge becomes present agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the named subject in this ayah to the prior question about divine knowledge (29:10).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL boundary row gives the prior reference, and local syntax turns the already invoked divine knowledge into an explicit subject-predicate act.

words.gloss_range: masculine plural relative pronoun forming the object phrase whose defining clause follows
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) does not give the first object as a bare label. It opens a relative phrase whose following action defines the group, so the first side of the binary is known through enacted belief rather than a static class-name.

topics.headline: object opened by relative pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first object is a clause-defined group, not a simple noun label.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the relative pronoun as the direct object of the knowing verb and the subject of the relative clause.

topics.headline: verb-defined believers against noun-defined opposite
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the first group defined by action, preparing the contrast with the final noun-class.
topics.reason: The two object slots are parallel, but the first is a relative clause and the second is a definite active participial noun.

words.gloss_range: completed plural believing in the relative clause, with trust/security pressure from the root and active Form IV participation
words.root_gloss_range: root range centers on safety, security, trust, faith, and giving credence; local Form IV perfect selects enacted belief as entry into trust
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) completes the relative object by naming what the group has done, with the plural subject carried inside the verb. Its perfect form makes the belief a completed claim or act now placed under future-certain divine distinction, answering the prior claim under pressure (29:10). The Form IV root pressure makes belief active entry into trust and security rather than bare opinion, and that trust stands opposite the concealed-exit field of the final class. A compact m/n sound thread links the knowing predicate and both classified groups.

topics.headline: plural verb completes the relative object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the believer group is grammatically completed inside the action of believing.
topics.reason: The verb agrees with the plural relative pronoun and supplies the predicate of the relative clause.

topics.headline: perfect belief under future-certain sorting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees a gap between the completed human claim of belief and the still-to-be-manifest divine sorting.
topics.reason: QAC marks this verb as perfect while the governing knowing verb is oath-bound imperfect with future certainty.

topics.headline: belief as active entry into trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief carries trust and security pressure, while the local clause still selects the act of believing.
topics.reason: The root is missing from V4 guardrail rows, so the coherent CRITICAL root pressure is preserved but kept subordinate to the local Form IV perfect verb.

topics.headline: trust root set against concealed-exit root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah's two object groups as a semantic opposition between trust/security and concealed exit, not only as social labels.
topics.reason: The two object terms occupy matched slots under repeated knowing verbs, and the supplied pairings support the local contrast.

topics.headline: faith placed under divine knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that belief is not merely named; it is the object of divine verification after the pressure of the prior claim (29:10).
topics.reason: The local syntax embeds the faith verb inside the object known by the divine subject, and the boundary row gives the prior contrast.

topics.headline: nasal sound links predicate and objects
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a compact sound thread binding the knowing verb and both classified groups.
topics.reason: The phonetic observation is local to the recited surfaces and adds a small but concrete auditory payoff.

words.gloss_range: mid-ayah conjunction that coordinates a fresh repeated oath clause rather than merely adding a second object
words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge of the ayah. It adds the second group, but it also separates that group into its own coordinated oath clause, restarting the same launch instead of letting the final object trail behind the first verb.

topics.headline: connector starts a separate oath clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second group receives its own sworn declaration, not a compressed add-on to the first.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the second verbal clause as coordinated with the first, not as a second object in the first clause.

topics.headline: midline pivot with repeated launch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the ayah turn from believers to hypocrites through the same connective doorway.
topics.reason: The same connector-plus-oath cadence returns at the beginning of the second half.

words.gloss_range: second oath-emphasis particle giving the hypocrite clause its own sworn scope
words.prose: The second {{ar:لَ}} ({{tr:la}}) repeats the oath force with a new target. It makes the exposure of the second group independently emphatic and formally balanced with the first classification beat, returning the same short-particle-to-heavy-closure pressure contour.

topics.headline: second group receives its own oath scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second clause is separately sworn over, not merely included under the first oath.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the second particle as the same oath lām, and the attachment evidence marks a second coordinated verbal assertion.

topics.headline: repeated particle keeps the clauses balanced
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the second classification as no weaker than the first because the same emphatic contour returns.
topics.reason: The repeated bound particle fuses to the repeated imperfect and recreates the first clause's formal pressure.

words.gloss_range: repeated sworn knowing verb, with the subject carried from the first clause and the object shifted to the concealed hypocrite class
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes knowing, recognizing, teaching or informing, and the sign or mark field; local repetition selects knowing as exposure and classification
words.prose: The second {{ar:يَعْلَمَنَّ}} ({{tr:yaʿlamanna}}) is not a reduced reprise. The subject is carried from the first clause, but the full emphatic verb returns so the second object receives the same predicate force and the same held emphatic closure. Because the object is the concealed class, knowing now feels especially like exposure. The repeated formula also completes the testing reprise (29:3) by naming the negative pole after the believer pole.

topics.headline: subject ellipsis shifts focus to object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine agent is already fixed, so the second clause can compress toward the newly named object.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence notes the implicit subject in the second verb and the explicit subject supplied by the first clause.

topics.headline: full emphatic verb repeated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the second judgment is formally complete and not dependent on a lighter anaphoric construction.
topics.reason: The second clause repeats the full imperfect plus heavy emphasis instead of using only a coordinated object.

topics.headline: knowing sharpens into exposure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same knowing verb becomes sharper when aimed at a class defined by concealment.
topics.reason: The local direct object is the hypocrite class, so the supported mark-and-knowledge pressure is narrowed to exposure rather than a free root-wide expansion.

topics.headline: same predicate distributed over opposed classes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the ayah as two matched passes of the same classification act, with only the object class changing.
topics.reason: The two verbs have identical morphology and parallel object positions in coordinated clauses.

topics.headline: reprise names the negative pole
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the second repeated verb to the earlier testing formula (29:3), now completed by the negative class.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL row supplies the concrete 29:3 reference, and the local second clause names the negative pole after the believer pole.

topics.headline: second heavy closure matches the first
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears that the second classification is acoustically no weaker than the first.
topics.reason: The final heavy emphasis is repeated in the second verb's recited form.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural active participial class, the exposed object of the second knowing verb
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes passing away or depletion, spending as wealth going out, tunnel or passage with an exit, and hypocrisy as showing one face while concealing another; local noun selects the hypocrisy class with concealed-exit pressure
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُنَٰفِقِينَ}} ({{tr:al-munāfiqīn}}) lands as the ayah's final object and exposed negative class, grammatically locked into the same object architecture as the first group. Its definite active participial plural names an established practiced role, and its Form III pressure makes hypocrisy relational rather than solitary. The root's passage-and-hidden-exit field makes the label more concrete than inward insincerity alone, with depletion and pass-through pressure kept secondary to the local hypocrisy sense. The canonical wording stays tightly binary: believers are distinguished, and this concealed class is exposed. Across the local sequence, the word names the exposed result of testing (29:2-3), resolves the prior portrait (29:10), and precedes open rejection in the next ayah (29:12). A nasal-and-long-vowel resemblance binds the opposed object terms while their roots divide them.

topics.headline: definite active participial object class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final object is a recognized practiced class, not an indefinite possibility or one-time act.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a definite active participle in the direct-object slot of the second knowing verb.

topics.headline: oblique plural fits the object slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final class grammatically locked into the same object architecture as the first group.
topics.reason: The sound masculine plural oblique form fits the accusative object role governed by the repeated verb.

topics.headline: hypocrisy as hidden-route practice
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the hypocrite label as a concealed-route practice: one visible entrance with another way out.
topics.reason: V4 supports the tunnel and hypocrisy branches, while local grammar selects the active participial hypocrisy class rather than making every root branch independently active.

topics.headline: passage-through pressure beside hypocrisy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a secondary passage-through and depletion pressure that thickens the label without replacing its local hypocrisy sense.
topics.reason: The depletion and expenditure branches are real root-family evidence, but the local active participle selects the hypocrisy branch, so these pressures remain subordinate.

topics.headline: variant highlights canonical binary scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the received wording keeps divine knowledge focused on two named classes instead of expanding the statement into universal scope.
topics.reason: The variant is useful as apparatus because it contrasts with the canonical two-object structure, but it does not control the local parse.

topics.headline: covert class before open rejection
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final word distinguish covert rejection here from open rejection in the following ayah (29:12).
topics.reason: The supplied rows give the concrete adjacent reference, and the local word names the covert class before the next ayah names open rejection.

topics.headline: negative pole against trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the final noun-class as the negative pole against the earlier trust/belief phrase.
topics.reason: The word is the second object under the repeated knowing verb and stands opposite the action-defined believer phrase.

topics.headline: fitnah-testing arc reaches named result
topics.reader_payoff: The reader connects the final label to the testing frame at the surah opening (29:2-3).
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows give concrete references to 29:2-3, and the final word names the exposed outcome of that testing discourse.

topics.headline: closure lands on exposed negative class
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the ayah land not on neutral classification but on the exposed concealed class.
topics.reason: The final word position, definite class form, and root image converge to make exposure the landing point.

topics.headline: prior portrait becomes judicial category
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the behavior sketched in the prior ayah (29:10) resolved into a definite class-name.
topics.reason: The boundary rows tie the final label to the prior unnamed pattern and show the register shift into oath-governed classification.

topics.headline: sound resemblance binds opposed classes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears a sound resemblance between the two opposed object terms even as their roots separate them.
topics.reason: The sound observation is local to the two object terms and adds an auditory layer to the semantic opposition.

topics.headline: Form III agency as practiced role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices hypocrisy as an agentive practiced role, while the local noun form keeps that role in the definite class label.
topics.reason: QAC supports the active participial class from Form III; broader claims about reciprocity are kept as role pressure rather than an independent local construction.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The doubled emphatic knowing construction places believers and hypocrites under matching acts of divine knowing.
baseline_models.mechanism: Parallel clauses make knowing an assured disclosure of two inwardly opposed alignments: settled assent and a displayed identity concealing its contrary.

activation_trace.role: Uncovering supplies the repeated act that renders both alignments fully known.
Heart-settling assent supplies the positive inward alignment.
A shown entrance with a concealed contrary exit supplies the negative inward-outward mismatch.

changed_reading.after: The balanced double assertion guarantees disclosure of settled assent and concealed contrary alignment.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The opposed objects rooted in ء م ن and ن ف ق carry contrasting security and passage images.
baseline_models.mechanism: Faith organizes the interior as settled trust; hypocrisy organizes identity as a passage with one route presented and another hidden. The contrast is coherence versus strategic reversibility, not merely two labels.

activation_trace.role: Security and heart-settling trust supply a stable inward center.
A through-tunnel with an outlet supplies reversible routing through identity.
The visible entrance and concealed exit make that routing socially asymmetric.

changed_reading.before: Believers are sincere and hypocrites are insincere.
changed_reading.after: Belief is settled trust, while hypocrisy is a dual-route posture able to enter publicly and leave covertly.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same ع ل م verb is emphatically repeated for each contrasted object.
baseline_models.mechanism: The root's distinguishing-mark branch lets the repetition suggest diagnostic identification: concealed difference is not left unmarked before divine knowing.

activation_trace.role: A distinguishing trace that guides recognition supplies a diagnostic sense of knowing.
Concealed contradiction creates the condition requiring diagnostic discernment.

changed_reading.before: The two classes are simply known.
changed_reading.after: The repeated knowing also detects the distinguishing trace that defeats concealed contradiction.

context_deltas.mechanism: Testing is an assay that turns a verbal claim into a manifested result. The near-exact double-knowing frame in 29:3 couples assay to firmness and truth, revising 29:11 from static cognition into disclosure through trial.

activation_trace.role: Repeated uncovering is the focus mechanism revised by the assay sequence.
The assay of metal or person makes testing the process applied to a stated identity.
The same doubled uncovering construction links completed trial to contrasted outcomes.
Firmness and evenness supply the property that survives assay and becomes readable as truth.

structural_cues: 29:2 places the claim of belief before the expectation of testing.
29:3 repeats 29:11's two emphatic knowing clauses but names truthful and lying outcomes.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies claim, assay, firmness, and repeated syntax; I supply the arrow from testing to manifestation rather than acquisition of absent divine information. Timeless cognition remains a live alternative.

changed_reading.before: Divine knowledge passively contains the two identities.
changed_reading.after: Trial functions as an assay through which settled or divided alignment becomes manifest under assured discriminating knowledge.

context_deltas.mechanism: In 29:10 two affiliation claims bracket opposite pressures: harm dislodges the speaker, while visible aid draws a claim of prior solidarity. The hidden outlet becomes a pressure-sensitive routing mechanism whose source lies in the chest.

activation_trace.role: Settled trust supplies the pressure-resistant pole.
A through-passage supplies an alternate route when conditions change.
The shown entrance and hidden outlet explain selective presentation of contrary affiliations.
Two uttered claims provide the public surfaces on either side of the pressure change.
Harm that prevents settledness supplies destabilizing pressure.
Ordeal supplies the adverse condition under which affiliation bends.
Aid and its emergence supply the favorable condition eliciting the second claim.
The chest as source of acts locates hidden routing beneath the claims.

structural_cues: 29:10 conditionally sequences profession, injury, reassessment, victory, and renewed profession immediately before 29:11.
Its closing question about knowledge of chests feeds directly into the focus's doubled knowing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies changing pressures, paired claims, and the chest as source; I infer that the switches expose the concealed outlet. Temporary fear without settled hypocrisy remains an alternative.

changed_reading.before: A hypocrite says one thing while inwardly believing another.
changed_reading.after: Hypocritical identity is exposed when affiliation reroutes toward whichever source of harm or aid currently dominates.

context_deltas.mechanism: The contrast between settled security and a concealed tunnel expands into rival refuge architectures. Alternate patrons construct an apparently protective dwelling that lacks strength; knowing exposes which shelter actually organizes allegiance.

activation_trace.role: Security and settled trust supply the desired function of refuge.
The tunnel supplies covert architecture for alternate escape routes.
Patronage, love, and aid supply the social material of the alternate refuge.
Dwelling and shelter turn patronage into an explicit protective structure.
Weak force and slack resolve disclose structural failure under load.
Knowing as uncovering closes the simile by exposing the refuge's actual strength.

structural_cues: 29:41 joins alternate patrons, a house, structural weakness, and knowing in one simile.
The focus roots independently supply security and a tunnel with a concealed outlet.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies security, tunnel, patronage, shelter, weakness, and knowing; I map inward allegiance onto refuge design. The house may instead target idolatrous alliance generally.

changed_reading.before: Belief and hypocrisy differ as sincere versus concealed conviction.
changed_reading.after: They also model rival refuge systems: settled trust versus weak patronage preserved by covert escape routes.

context_deltas.mechanism: Clear signs located in chests and denial that can coexist with knowledge strengthen the diagnostic-mark baseline. Divine knowing discerns not only propositions held but the relation between interior signs and outward response.

structural_cues: 29:49 sequences signs, clarity, chests, knowledge, and denial.
The focus repeats knowing over a contrast whose negative member hides contrary alignment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies interior signs, disclosure, knowledge, and knowledgeable denial; I infer that these traces function diagnostically. The mark branch may remain only an etymological resonance.

changed_reading.before: Divine knowing reads an inaccessible inward state.
changed_reading.after: It also discerns how interior signs issue into acknowledgment or knowledgeable denial, making concealed difference legible.

context_deltas.mechanism: Sea-to-land movement alternates exclusive obedience and renewed association, while the next secure-boundary scene joins safety to misdirected belief. Genuine trust remains coherent across danger and safety; divided allegiance flips at thresholds.

structural_cues: 29:65 explicitly sequences boarding, exclusive invocation, rescue, and immediate association.
29:67 places secure sanctuary, snatching outside, and belief in falsehood in one contrast.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies thresholds, exclusive obedience, reversal, sanctuary, and danger; I infer that stability across transitions diagnoses the focus contrast. Broader episodic polytheism remains an alternative.

changed_reading.before: Believer and hypocrite are static identity classes.
changed_reading.after: They are dynamically legible by transition behavior: settled trust stays coherent, while divided allegiance uses thresholds as entrances and exits.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This surprisingly extends the expenditure branch of ن ف ق into moral accounting and uses neighboring disbeliever speech, not an explicit definition of hypocrisy. It remains anchored in the focus noun and the immediate sequence's promised transfer, actual weights, and fabricated claim. Render it only as a concealed-liability analogy, not a lexical gloss.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus noun rooted in ن ف ق can activate outflow or expenditure alongside its ordinary concealed-exit branch.

activation_trace.role: Expenditure and loss from outflow supply the exploratory accounting frame.

changed_reading.before: Hypocrisy conceals conviction contrary to a claim.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it also resembles hidden liability accounting: offering to route moral cost away while the concealed account gains weight.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the crafted-bearing branch of ص ن ع is form-distant and 29:45 does not name hypocrites. It remains anchored through the focus's displayed entrance and hidden contrary exit, while 29:45 repeats divine knowing beside what people fashion. Render it as a performative-image activation, not a claim that practice is artificial.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus pairs repeated divine knowing with a noun whose branch inventory foregrounds a displayed entrance concealing another route.

activation_trace.role: Uncovering supplies penetration of a fashioned public surface.
The displayed entrance and concealed outlet anchor presentation versus route.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the hypocrite fashions a readable religious surface whose construction remains transparent to divine knowing.

strongest_changes: The opening assay turns knowing from static possession of facts into manifestation and discrimination under trial.
The harm-and-victory and sea-to-land sequences expose divided allegiance through pressure-sensitive switching.
Weak-house, secure-sanctuary, and sign-in-chest scenes recast the contrast as refuge design and diagnostically legible inward-outward relation.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context made the focus roots behave as mechanisms rather than labels: assay, settled security, concealed tunnels, weak shelters, interior signs, and threshold crossings converged on how allegiance becomes manifest.
remaining_uncertainties: The distinguishing-mark branch of ع ل م may be resonance rather than an active sense of the focus verb.
Ship, sanctuary, and weak-house scenes describe broader divided worship and may not map exclusively onto technical hypocrisy.
Liability-transfer and crafted-persona readings remain contained cross-domain analogies.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Exit-bearing duplicity made visible.** ن ف ق B003 is a tunnel or burrow with an exit; B004 is “showing one face while concealing another exit.” Repeated knowing separates believers from hypocrites immediately after the pressure-driven shifts of 29:10. I infer that trial reveals the concealed escape route by which public belonging can be abandoned; hypocrisy reads as a structure built with a second exit, not merely a false sentence.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The ship crisis in 29:65 reveals exclusive devotion and the shore restores association, giving the concealed-exit image a temporal form: one allegiance surfaces under danger and another exits into view under safety.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Knowing becomes the exposure of two allegiance structures.** Lexical evidence: repeated `لَيَعْلَمَنَّ`, root `ع ل م`, `B002` (a distinguishing mark that points to something), and `ٱلْمُنَافِقِينَ`, root `ن ف ق`, `B004` (showing one face while concealing another exit). Structural cue: `29:10` supplies the two contrary speeches generated by harm and aid; `29:12` supplies another attractive public promise that conceals failed liability. Assigned role: the tunnel-image of hypocrisy explains how one displayed entrance can preserve a hidden exit, while knowledge marks the actual structure. Abductive move: I infer from the repeated future-emphatic verb and the adjacent behavioral switches that knowing is enacted as differentiation, not acquisition of missing information. Reading change: believers and hypocrites become visibly separable modes of allegiance.

2. **Security is tested against the concealed exit.** Lexical evidence: `ءَامَنُوا`, root `ء م ن`, `B001` (settled security and trust), opposed structurally to `ن ف ق B004`. Structural cue: the preceding person changes affiliation under injury and victory, whereas the following invitation asks believers to follow another route. Assigned role: settled trust removes the need for an emergency exit; hypocrisy keeps one available. Abductive move: the packet does not say trust physically blocks hypocrisy, so the directional contrast is mine, inferred from stability versus hidden egress. Reading change: faith here reads as settled relational security demonstrated by not changing exits with circumstance.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: - **Later activation (`29:65`, `29:67`):** Crisis-only purity followed by safe-land association gives the hidden-exit image of `ن ف ق B004` a concrete late form; sanctuary then shows trust attached to voidness despite lived security. Manifest differentiation therefore concerns durable object-attachment across states.

Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, kişinin içinde taşıdığının tersini göstermesini ve özellikle inanç alanında dışarıdan bağlı görünürken gizlice bu bağlılığın dışında kalmasını aynı çekirdekte birleştirir. Yer altı geçidiyle kurulan adlandırma bağlantısı açıklayıcı bir benzetidir; dalın tanımı fiziksel geçit değil, saklanan iç tutum ile gösterilen dış tutum arasındaki karşıtlıktır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, içte saklanan inanç veya tutumun tersini dışarıya gösterme durumudur; genel aldatma, gösteriş ve açıkça inançtan dönme bununla özdeş değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalın anlamıyla iç tutumun tersini dışarıya gösterme ve inançta gizli ayrılık çekirdeğinde tanımlanır; başka dallardaki geçit veya harcama anlamları içeri alınmaz.

concept_map.definition: Kişinin içindeki inanç veya tutumun tersini dışarıya göstermesi, bir bağlılığa girmiş görünürken ondan gizlice ayrı kalmasıdır. Dış görünüş ile saklanan iç durum arasındaki bilinçli karşıtlık dalın kurucu özelliğidir.

facets.statement: Kişi, içinde sakladığı inanç veya tutumun tersini dışarıya gösterir.
İnanç alanında kişi dışarıdan bağlı görünürken içten inanmamayı veya karşıtlığı saklar.
Durum, bir bağlılığa bir kapıdan girip başka bir kapıdan gizlice çıkma görüntüsüyle açıklanır.
Adlandırma, gizli bir çıkışı bulunan yer altı geçidi görüntüsüyle ilişkilendirilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, kişinin içindeki karşıtlığı veya inanmamayı saklayıp dışarıya başka bir bağlılık göstermesini merkez alır. Bir kapıdan girip diğerinden gizlice çıkma ve gizli çıkışlı yer altı geçidi görüntüleri, iç durum ile dış görünüş arasındaki bu ayrılığı açıklar.
